tools.name: anyhook_mock
tools.description: Generate a webhook request with a valid signature for Stripe, GitHub, or Slack. If targetUrl is provided, the request is POSTed there and the response is returned.

tools.name: anyhook_verify
tools.description: Verify a webhook signature against a secret. Supports 20 providers including stripe, github, shopify, slack, line, discord, linear, vercel, paddle, hubspot, and paypal.

tools.name: anyhook_providers
tools.description: List webhook providers AnyHook can mock, along with the event types available for each.

tools.name: anyhook_apps_list
tools.description: List apps in your AnyHook account with inbound URLs, sources, and destination URLs. Check isActive: an inactive app's inbound URL answers setup handshakes but acknowledges and discards event POSTs (202, reason app_inactive) instead of relaying them. Destination signing secrets are redacted to has_si

tools.name: anyhook_inbox
tools.description: Every AnyHook app is also an email inbox: mail sent to {user}.{app}@anyhook.net becomes an event (type email.received) you can read with anyhook_events. Returns the address and webhook URL for one of your apps.

tools.name: anyhook_apps_create
tools.description: Create a new app with a name, provider source, and (optionally) destinations. Returns the inbound URL. The app is active immediately. Created WITHOUT destinations it still receives and LOGS every event (inspect-only), it just delivers nowhere until a destination is added (PATCH /api/v1/apps/{slug} w

tools.name: anyhook_replay
tools.description: Re-send a stored event to its destinations. Replay does not consume monthly event quota, but the destination does run its handler again: a receiver that is not idempotent will process the event twice while debugging.

tools.name: anyhook_undelivered
tools.description: Show events for the given app that have not successfully reached any destination (failed or still retrying).

tools.name: anyhook_replay_failed
tools.description: Re-send every failed event for the given app slug. Useful after fixing a downstream bug to recover queued work.

tools.name: anyhook_events
tools.description: List webhook events, most recent first: id, app, type, status, attempt, destination status code, latency, timestamp. Summaries only, no request headers or body — call anyhook_inspect with an id from here to read one event's payload. Uses your AnyHook account when connected, otherwise the local in-me

tools.name: anyhook_inspect
tools.description: Full detail for one event by id, including the inbound headers and body that anyhook_events omits, plus the destination's response. Payloads can be large and often contain personal data, so fetch one at a time, only when the body is needed. Account or local store.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: anyhook_apps_list, anyhook_inbox · Private data: anyhook_verify, anyhook_apps_list · Public sink: anyhook_mock, anyhook_verify, anyhook_providers, anyhook_inbox, anyhook_replay, anyhook_replay_failed, anyhook_events · Destructive: anyhook_replay.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: anyhook_apps_list, anyhook_inbox · Private data: anyhook_verify, anyhook_apps_list · Public sink: anyhook_mock, anyhook_verify, anyhook_providers, anyhook_inbox, anyhook_replay, anyhook_replay_failed, anyhook_events · Destructive: anyhook_replay

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
